business: SIR'OTÉ by SAS Sir'Ose: Koso fermented syrup for bars and hotels in Réunion island
target: The person who chooses and orders cocktail syrups (head bartender, bar manager or F&B manager) in a hotel, cocktail bar or restaurant bar in Réunion island

segments.name: Head bartender in an independent cocktail bar or beach bar (pays in euros, salary shown)
Bar manager in a restaurant or bistro with a short cocktail list (salary in euros)
F&B manager or head of bar in a 3 to 5 star hotel (salary in euros)
Owner-operator of a small bar or snack bar who orders everything himself (income in euros)

behaviours.name: Monin loyalist
behaviours.how: Orders Monin through the usual distributor with the rest of the stock; values consistency and never running out.

behaviours.name: Margin-first
behaviours.how: Calculates the cost of every cocktail and cuts anything that raises it without raising the menu price.

behaviours.name: Craft and local
behaviours.how: Already makes some syrups or rhums arrangés in-house and likes putting péi producers on the menu.

behaviours.name: Mocktail builder
behaviours.how: Is growing the no-alcohol list because more guests ask for it, looking for less sugary bases.

behaviours.name: Brand-standard hotel buyer
behaviours.how: Has to go through purchasing, needs invoices, labels, allergen sheets and a reliable supplier.

behaviours.name: Trend chaser
behaviours.how: Changes the signature cocktails every season and posts them on Instagram.

behaviours.name: Time-poor
behaviours.how: Short-staffed in high season, wants anything that saves prep time behind the bar.

objections: 23 euros a litre is two to three times what I pay for Monin
Will it taste the same from one batch to the next?
A small producer might run out of stock in high season
It is fermented: how long does it keep once opened, and does it need the fridge?
My guests order a mojito or a ti-punch, not a Koso
I can make my own syrups and rhums arrangés
Is it alcoholic? I need to know for the no-alcohol menu and the paperwork
Returning deposit bottles is one more thing to manage
habits: you work evenings and weekends, peak season is December to February and July-August
your bar sells between 30 and 150 cocktails on a busy night
the hotel or owner reviews the cost of the drinks list every quarter
you already buy rum from Réunion distilleries and syrups from one main distributor
you follow other Réunion bartenders on Instagram
